key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with tuned DDFW settings substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance from process conditions.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical path to stronger lightweight aluminum joints for aerospace and automotive applications by linking joint design with process optimization and AI-based prediction.
method: Used an L18 orthogonal array to test friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time.
Compared conventional flat-to-flat joints with a drilled-to-bossed geometry inspired by mortise-and-tenon interlocking.
Trained deep learning models, including an ensemble residual network, compact attention network, and adaptive multiscale network, to predict ultimate tensile strength.
evidence_signal: The best setting produced 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the top predictor achieved about R² = 0.81.
watch_item: The reported prediction accuracy is moderate, so broader validation on more datasets and weld conditions would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
